environment.base_gridworld module

Base GridWorld environment for Dyna-Q reinforcement learning.

Provides core grid navigation mechanics, deterministic transition dynamics, coordinate mappings, and collision detection.

class environment.base_gridworld.BaseGridWorld(grid: List[List[int]], start_pos: Tuple[int, int], goal_pos: Tuple[int, int], step_reward: float = -1.0, goal_reward: float = 10.0, collision_reward: float | None = None, max_steps: int = 2000, wall_value: int = 1, path_value: int = 0)

Bases: object

Base 2D GridWorld navigation environment.

Represents a rectangular grid where an agent navigates from a start state to a goal state while avoiding wall obstacles.

Actions:

0: UP (-1, 0) 1: DOWN ( 1, 0) 2: LEFT ( 0, -1) 3: RIGHT ( 0, 1)

environment.gridworld_standard module

Standard GridWorld environment without affective monitoring.

This environment implements the standard Dyna-Q reinforcement learning benchmark without internal Valence-Arousal emotion dynamics or frequency memory tracking.

class environment.gridworld_standard.StandardGridWorld(grid: List[List[int]], start_pos: Tuple[int, int], goal_pos: Tuple[int, int], step_reward: float = -1.0, goal_reward: float = 10.0, max_steps: int = 2000, wall_value: int = 1, path_value: int = 0)

Bases: BaseGridWorld

Standard GridWorld environment.

Used for baseline Dyna-Q benchmarks using static or exponentially decaying parameters without affective state calculations.

environment.gridworld_va_ann module

Affective GridWorld environment for Artificial Neural Network (ANN) integration.

Provides sensory signals and reward modification hooks for neural network-based affect appraisal without parameter modulation.

class environment.gridworld_va_ann.ANNGridWorld(grid: List[List[int]], start_pos: Tuple[int, int], goal_pos: Tuple[int, int], step_reward: float = -1.0, goal_reward: float = 10.0, max_steps: int = 2000, wall_value: int = 1, path_value: int = 0, reward_modifier: Callable[[float, float, float], float] | None = None)

Bases: BaseGridWorld

GridWorld designed for neural network-based affective reward shaping.

Captures low-level sensory signals (collision, direction changes, Bresenham visibility, distance progression) and provides an interface for an ANN model to predict affective values (Valence, Arousal) and modulate rewards.

Optional callback (original_reward, valence, arousal) -> modified_reward.

Optional[Callable[[float, float, float], float]]

environment.gridworld_va_classic module

Affective-monitored GridWorld using classic Valence-Arousal dynamics.

Implements sensory tracking (collision, direction change, Bresenham line of sight, and distance from start) and discrete dynamical frequency calculations according to Feldmaier and Diepold (2014).

class environment.gridworld_va_classic.ClassicVAGridWorld(grid: List[List[int]], start_pos: Tuple[int, int], goal_pos: Tuple[int, int], step_reward: float = -1.0, goal_reward: float = 10.0, collision_reward: float = -5.0, max_steps: int = 2000, wall_value: int = 1, path_value: int = 0, nu: float = 0.2, theta1: float = 0.2, theta2: float = 0.2, kappa: float = 0.15, bias_reward_with_affect: bool = False)

Bases: BaseGridWorld

GridWorld environment with integrated Valence-Arousal sensory monitoring.

Tracks environmental events and reflection-level emotional states:

  • Collision detection with walls/boundaries (c)

  • Direction change monitoring (d)

  • Bresenham line-of-sight raycasting to the goal (g)

  • Distance progression from the starting location (i)

affect

Core affect dynamical model.

Type:

ClassicValenceArousal

bias_reward_with_affect

If True, sets non-terminal reward to 0 when valence > 0 (Feldmaier & Diepold experiment 2).

Type:

bool

reset(seed: int | None = None) → Tuple[int, Dict[str, Any]]

seed (Optional[int], optional) – Optional seed. Defaults to None.

Returns:

Return type:

Tuple[int, Dict[str, Any]]

Module contents

GridWorld reinforcement learning environments.

Provides base environment and specialized environments for standard Dyna-Q, classic Feldmaier-Diepold affective states, and ANN affective reward models.
